intro: Three people made the decisions; agents and generators did most of the making. Below is every group of AI-made assets in the game: which tool and model made it, what it is for, what it cost, the prompt we actually sent, and what came out wrong first. Open a prompt to read it word for word.

groups.title: Claude Code: the director's chair
groups.what_for: Claude Code agents wrote the C++ and tests, built levels through Unreal MCP, and drove every other generator below through MCP servers and REST APIs, writing a meta.json with prompts, seeds and costs next to each asset.
groups.tools: Claude Code (Anthropic) with Claude Code Game Studios (our MIT set of agents, skills and hooks), Unreal MCP in UE 5.9, MCP servers for Meshy, Hyper3D Rodin and Tripo, fal.ai and ElevenLabs over their APIs, headless Blender 5.3 and UE editor Python scripts
groups.count: Many parallel agents, each in its own git worktree; one integrator owned main. Examples from the dev log: six agents at once on Day 1, five more waves that night, nineteen issues on fourteen branches on Day 2, eleven read-only audit agents at once on Day 3; about 300 automated tests after Day 1, 605 of 605 green for rc-1311d.

prompts.label: Day 1, from call notes to a plan (translated from Polish in the dev log)
prompts.text: use the game-making skills from the studio, analyse Badys's notes and the call transcript

prompts.label: Day 0, prompt of the night
prompts.text:
Check the prompt templates against each vendor's official documentation.
Where the docs say nothing, write that down instead of guessing.

prompts.label: Day 3, rules shared by all eleven audit agents (excerpt as printed in the dev log)
prompts.text:
READ-ONLY on D:\gra: do not edit, commit, build or stash in the D:\gra working tree (other agents use it). Do not ask questions.
If you need to run the editor/game or build, create your OWN worktree [...]
Output: ranked findings P0/P1/P2 with evidence (file:line, numbers, log lines, screenshot paths), one-line fix, size S/M/L.

groups.went_wrong: Two parallel test runs picked up each other's tests, so one agent's green result came from another agent's code (fixed with a unique -SessionId per run). Around 13:40 on Day 2 a group of agent sessions stopped at once on an authentication error; because every agent commits after each finished task, a restart cost at most the task in progress. A performance agent once switched ray tracing off for weak PCs, which would have cost us the NVIDIA RTX Award, so we turned it back on for RTX cards.

groups.title: Pickups: things you carry
groups.what_for: The items players pick up, carry, sell or throw: film reels, batteries, flashlight, camcorder, rubber duck, trumpet, scanner, book, watch, trophy, clapperboard, empty reel, walkie-talkie and flash camera.
groups.tools: Day 1: Meshy text to image (nano-banana-pro, gpt-image-2 for the reel) -> Meshy Image to 3D (meshy-t2.5 smart topology + meshy-7 PBR texture) or Hyper3D Rodin Gen-2.5-Medium. Day 3 batch (#228): fal-ai/nano-banana reference -> Meshy Image to 3D (meshy-t2 smart topology + meshy-n1 texture); Blender Decimate to 5k triangles
groups.count: 15 item models with meta.json: 5 from Day 1 (large battery, flashlight, camcorder, reel, rubber duck) and 10 from the #228 batch
groups.cost: #228 batch: 150 Meshy credits and about 0.45 USD on fal. Day 1 items per meta.json: 114 Meshy credits (battery 33, flashlight 24, camcorder 18, reel 30, duck 9); Rodin credits not reported by the Rodin MCP.

prompts.label: SM_Trumpet (#228, shared style prefix + object, fal-ai/nano-banana)
prompts.text: Product photo of one single object on a plain light-grey seamless background, soft even studio lighting, three-quarter view from slightly above, the whole object visible and centered with margin around it. prompts.label: SM_Val_Clapperboard (#228)
prompts.text: Product photo of one single object on a plain light-grey seamless background, soft even studio lighting, three-quarter view from slightly above, the whole object visible and centered with margin around it. prompts.label: Bus body (FLUX.2 [pro] edit, style refs @image1..@image3)
prompts.text: A single very long boxy 1960s high-roof film crew van, an extended delivery bus body about three times longer than it is tall, with a flat roof and a long cargo section behind the cab. Made in the exact stylized art style of the objects in @image1, @image2 and @image3: a game asset with chunky, slightly faceted, hand-carved looking shapes, deep panel seams, bright worn highlights hand-painted along every edge and seam, small scratches, dents and rivets, simple readable forms, not photorealistic. Mustard yellow paint like the duck in @image1 with a wide cream stripe along the side, burnt copper bumpers, hubcaps, window frames and an empty roof rack like the metal in @image2, round chrome headlights, a large sliding side door on the right side of the cargo section, two rear doors, small dark tinted windows you cannot see through, dark brown tyres. No text, no logos, no lettering, no license plate. Seen from the front right at a three-quarter angle, the whole van fully visible and centered with space around it, on a plain dark charcoal grey background with soft, even studio lighting.

prompts.label: Defibrillator
prompts.text: A single vintage 1960s wall-mounted defibrillator kit for a film crew van: a sturdy rectangular metal wall cabinet painted cream and faded teal with burnt copper trim and hinges, its front door open, inside a chunky old defibrillator machine with a big round analog dial, two toggle switches, a small red indicator lamp and two heavy paddles with black handles hanging on coiled cables, and on the top panel a simple white heart with a lightning bolt symbol, [the same style sentence as above]. No text, no letters, no red cross, no logo.

groups.went_wrong: The first bus pictures looked like a photo of a real, short van; one result of the second round had a star badge that read as a real car brand. fal would not draw a CRT as wide as the desk in three tries, so Blender scaled the monitor islands 1.4x, and Rodin's defibrillator cabinet came out turned 33 degrees. A red phone booth was tried for the revive point and replaced by the defibrillator.

A 1970s film crew member (grip / camera assistant), adult man of average build, neutral calm expression, generic ordinary face that does not resemble any real person, short hair under a faded olive-green baseball cap. Worn tan canvas work jacket with sewn-on plain patches without any text, logos or brands, sleeves to the wrists, jacket closed. Old over-ear headphones with a coiled cable resting around the neck. Leather utility belt with a roll of grey gaffer tape clipped on the hip and a small leather pouch. Dark brown cargo trousers with side pockets, worn brown leather work boots. Muted 1970s colour palette, slightly dusty and worn fabric, realistic materials, game asset reference sheet, no props in hands, no text, no watermark.

groups.went_wrong: Rodin's first two rigging tries failed (wrong format, then a human_UE template without a Hips bone); the third with the 'human' template worked. groups.title: Take Fourteen, the monster
groups.what_for: The game's only monster: a gaunt 240 cm figure of wound magnetic film tape with a rusty reel hub in its chest, ear loops of film strip and two antennae, with 13 animations on one rig.
groups.tools: fal FLUX.2 [pro] (seed 1414) reference -> fal-ai/nano-banana/edit cleanup -> Meshy Image to 3D via REST (meshy-t2.5 smart topology, 22,225 triangles, meshy-n1 texture) -> Meshy Rig (24 bones) -> 8 Meshy Animate library clips + 5 Meshy Text to Motion clips; Blender removed root motion

groups.cost: 102 Meshy credits and about 0.10 USD on fal

prompts.label: Reference (FLUX.2 [pro], as stored in meta.json with ellipses)
prompts.text: Full-body character concept for a 3D game model, front view, symmetrical T-pose ... A gaunt, very tall humanoid creature (about 240 cm) built entirely from tangled brown magnetic film tape and old film-reel parts ... two large oval ear-like loops made of looped film tape with dusty pale pink membrane inside, and two long thin antenna-like stalks with cream tips ... Smooth eyeless face ... horror for teens, no gore, no blood, no text, no logos, single character only.

prompts.label: Cleanup (nano-banana/edit)
prompts.text: Edit this creature for a clean 3D game model: keep exactly the same character ... Remove every loose hanging strand of tape ... Move the two ear loops so they attach directly to the sides of the head ... completely eyeless and smooth ... symmetrical A-pose ... plain flat light-grey background, no text.

prompts.label: AN_Monster_Lunge (Text to Motion)
prompts.text: Crouches low and coils, then leaps forward in one short powerful lunge with both long arms reaching out to grab, and lands crouched.

prompts.label: AN_Monster_Idle_Listen (Text to Motion)
prompts.text: A tall creature stands still, slightly hunched forward, arms hanging loose, and slowly tilts its head to one side as if listening intently, holds, then slowly tilts its head to the other side and holds again.

groups.went_wrong: The text-to-motion lunge jumped 1.6 m into the air, so Blender lowered it (x0.3), and two sideways library clips were turned to face forward. Loose tape strands that would have ruined the rig were edited out of the reference. The first Unreal import renamed the skeleton and left the monster frozen in its A-pose until we imported onto a throwaway skeleton copy.

notes: Images: in this worktree most PNGs under Art/ and production/ are Git LFS pointers (about 130 bytes; the newest crew files are real), with the real files in the main checkout (D:/gra). size_kb is the real size read from the LFS pointer; most are 0.5 to 2 MB, so downscale for the web. All listed paths were checked to exist. The crew character (#227) was merged into this worktree's branch while the research ran (HEAD moved to 466bab2b); its files and docs are included. docs/tools-used.md lists the cinema facade among Rodin models, but Art/Source/Environment/SM_Facade_Cinema/meta.json (#232) says the current facade is a Blender box with a fal elevation image after two failed Meshy tries; an earlier Rodin facade may have existed and been replaced (not verified). Rodin credits are never reported (the Rodin MCP did not return them). Kling cost: 9.10 USD by price list, while the fal balance dropped 11.50 USD. Take Fourteen's FLUX.2 [pro] and cleanup prompts are stored in meta.json in abbreviated form with '...'; the full text is not in the repo. Prompts for the Listener's Day 1 animations were not found. Achievement badges and the Projection Booth UI kit are NOT AI-made (Python written by Claude Code); they are included because the brief expected them. Some HUD icons (book, dollar, mic, padlock, revive, etc.) are procedural too; only 12 icons are AI. Kling prompts in the video table are listed without the shared style suffix that was appended to each. Audio 'prompt' cells are quoted as written in assets/audio/generated.md, including the 'TTS eleven_v4, Bill...' prefix and Polish notes such as 'filtr głośnika' (loudspeaker filter). The studio day-1 count (26 meta.json files) differs from the dev log's '28 studio props'. On Day 1, brand names and a real film title appeared on three reference images that were thrown out; the sources name only the camcorder and the reel. Deliberately left out: the ElevenLabs voice id, Meshy/fal task and request ids, Rodin result URLs and signed Meshy thumbnail URLs found in meta.json.
